source_snapshot.test_name_items: Upgrade / Downgrade FPGA firmware by Redfish when system is off
source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Upgrade / Downgrade FPGA firmware through redfish.
1. Enter the command on the command line to set the behavior of BMC after update.
Command : curl -k -X PATCH https://root:0penBmc@${BMC_IP}/redfish/v1/UpdateService/ -H "Content-Type:application/json" -d '{"HttpPushUriOptions":{"HttpPushUriApplyTime":{"ApplyTime": "Immediate"}}}'
2. Change the name of the firmware file to be updated in the green text. This command may take some time to upload the firmware to BMC.
Command : curl -k -X POST https://root:0penBmc@${BMC_IP}/redfish/v1/UpdateService/update -H "Content-Type:application/octet-stream" --data-binary @${File_name}
3. Waiting for the flash progress complete.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
Firmware should be flashed successfully after BMC reset only one time.
curl -k -X GET https://root:0penBmc@${BMC_IP}/redfish/v1/UpdateService/FirmwareInventory

deepseek_columns.ai_packages_needed: curl (Redfish REST client, on the BMC side) + FPGA image (user provides)
deepseek_columns.ai_commands: -- FPGA downgrade via Redfish (system is off): the agent needs the exact user-provided FPGA image first the host must be powered OFF first (flash while system is off), then runs the Redfish update flow: `PATCH /redfish/v1/UpdateService` (set preserve/replace behavior), `POST /redfish/v1/UpdateService` to upload the image, poll the returned TaskService task to completion, then `GET /redfish/v1/UpdateService/FirmwareInventory` to confirm the new version is active. Not a single one-liner; run step-by-step after the image is placed on the BMC.
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return the full Redfish PATCH/POST response, the TaskService poll loop, and the final `FirmwareInventory` JSON so the user confirms the FPGA version changed and the SUT powers on cleanly after the off-state flash.
deepseek_columns.risk: RISK: FPGA firmware flash via Redfish is state-changing and can brick the BMC/host if interrupted; flash only the user-specified image with host powered off for a clean result, and never interrupt mid-flash.

historical_reviews.deepseek: PARTIAL; preserves the host-off FPGA API scope but reduces capability for input/approval and assumes generic Redfish behavior.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: BLOCKED / CHANGED; useful destructive controls, though the missing vendor/project contract is identifiable rather than irreducible.

original_test_intent: Automatically upgrade and downgrade the target FPGA through Redfish while the host is off, activate the image with the approved single-BMC-reset plan, and verify FPGA plus platform health after power-on.
original_method: Confirm host-off/BMC-standby state, PATCH apply behavior, POST an approved FPGA image, wait for terminal status, allow one BMC reset, query FirmwareInventory and then validate host/BMC/FPGA health.
manual_activity: An authorized engineer approves the exact component/image/reset/recovery plan and final verdict; approved Redfish, host-power and evidence interfaces can automate the full core lifecycle.
required_inputs: Exact FPGA/board/current/upgrade/downgrade versions and signed hashes
Vendor component-bound Redfish action, payload, task and apply semantics
Protected credentials, trusted CA and validated FPGA inventory mapping
Known-good recovery path and post-power-on criteria
safety_requirements: Reject embedded credentials and TLS bypass; authenticate securely to the verified BMC.
Require an advertised component selector or inventory binding so the FPGA—not another firmware member—receives the image.
Execute one approved transition/reset plan; never retry, reverse or add a cycle after uncertainty.
Maintain stable standby power and independent recovery; preserve task, reset, SEL and console failures.
agent_execution_scope: After approval, verify host-off state and FPGA identity, discover capabilities, submit one image, monitor the response-bound task/reset, then collect active FPGA inventory and host/BMC health after approved power-on.
Report raw status and differences without deciding the formal verdict.
engineer_actions: Approve device/image/order, one-reset activation behavior and recovery.
Evaluate FPGA and platform evidence and issue direction-specific verdicts.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The staged API lifecycle fits, but source URL credentials, `curl -k`, Immediate apply and `/update` are assumptions requiring vendor capability evidence. Image approval does not make the core partial.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use a secure, vendor-approved, capability-discovered component-bound update action; correlate the returned task and exactly one approved BMC reset before independent readback.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The host-off condition, source PATCH/POST/GET, one-reset criterion, script and 10/30-minute values remain.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Bind the signed image to the exact FPGA inventory member, discover the supported action/apply mode, execute one transition with response-correlated task and reset accounting, then verify active FPGA identity/version and post-power-on BMC/host/SEL health.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: BMC/FPGA combinations advertising vendor-approved FPGA update support.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record Redfish schema, BMC firmware, FPGA device/board/image, client/CA and recovery-tool versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Vendor Redfish FPGA update, activation and recovery documentation.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Removes credential/TLS and endpoint assumptions and adds component binding, task correlation and independent activation evidence.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Proves the intended programmable device became active and the system recovered, not only that upload returned success.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Generic FirmwareInventory may not uniquely identify board FPGA instances; project mapping must be validated.

project_override_considerations: Projects may define FPGA images, reset initiator/timing and automated host-power method. Completion is limited to the named device/version pair and observed one-reset plan.
expected_evidence: Approved FPGA board/device/image transition matrix and hashes
Redacted update response, response-bound task and one-reset timeline
Pre/post active FPGA inventory with validated device mapping
Post-power-on host POST/OS, BMC/SEL health and recovery readiness
Tool result separate from engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The source consistently targets FPGA via Redfish with host off and one BMC reset. Exact images, component mapping, reset initiator and action are project/vendor inputs, not contradictory facts.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The intended component lifecycle is identifiable. Unsafe literal commands can be replaced by a vendor-confirmed equivalent without changing scope; missing inputs affect readiness only.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Changes PARTIAL to FULLY AUTOMATABLE while retaining the host-off FPGA scope and correcting its endpoint/security assumptions.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Keeps safeguards but changes BLOCKED because the vendor/project inputs can define a safe state machine.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Separates automatable core, execution approval, tool result and engineer verdict.

review_improvement: Adds component binding and reset-correlated activation evidence to prevent generic inventory from proving the wrong FPGA.
independent_technical_reasoning: Host-state control, Redfish write/task tracking, BMC reset observation, inventory and platform checks are all automatable after a fixed approved plan. Destructive risk and missing images do not themselves reduce capability.
